facts.F27: Read model: TeamMetricsService reads through seven named reads on the owner repositories, not a query object per capability and not Flow-metrics ports in the module. W1 DoneItemsOfTeam(teamId), W2 DoingOrDoneItemsOfTeam(teamId), W3 ToDoOrDoingItemsOfTeam(teamId), W4 CountToDoOrDoingItemsOfTeam(teamId), W5 ItemsOfTeam(teamId) on IWorkItemRepository; T1 TransitionsOfWorkItems(IReadOnlyCollection<int> ids) on IWorkItemStateTransitionRepository; F1 FeaturesWithRealWorkForTeam(teamId, StateCategories? onlyIn) on IFeatureRepository. Reading goes through the owner's contract, so the owner keeps its one definition of how a Feature is read whole; no new dependency edge, no Program.cs edit, TeamMetricsService keeps its constructor. Names are working names; the crafter may improve them, but no new read may be called FeaturesOfTeam or FeaturesOfPortfolio.
facts.F28: Shape of a read: one named read per state-category set, each keeping today's predicate literally (Done; Doing or Done; ToDo or Doing; team only), with one private helper per repository holding the shared include and ordering code. A category set passed as a parameter or a StateCategorySet value object is rejected: it turns OR into IN over a parameter collection, and the row order of work-item reads is unspecified yet serialised per day in RunChartDataDto.WorkItemsPerUnitOfTime, so a new plan may reorder visible answers. W2 serves call sites written Done-or-Doing and Doing-or-Done.
facts.F29: Carriers and owners. Work-item reads (owner WorkItemRepository): Context.WorkItems.Include(Team).Where(today's predicate).ToList(), tracked, returned as IReadOnlyList<WorkItem>; W4 is a server-side Count() on the same query, returned as int, never load-and-count. Transition read (owner WorkItemStateTransitionRepository): Where(ids.Contains(WorkItemId)).ToList(), IReadOnlyList<WorkItemStateTransition>. Feature read (owner FeatureRepository): featureOrdering.Order(GetFeatures().Where(today's predicate).AsEnumerable()).ToList(), tracked, all five includes of GetFeatures(), IReadOnlyList<Feature>; F1 with onlyIn null serves the size chart, whose Done/ToDo/Doing filter stays in the service, in memory. No IQueryable, Expression or Func in a new signature. Tracking stays on, so identity and the Save in UpdateTeamMetrics see the same instances. Errors: a provider exception propagates unchanged; no new error type, retry or per-process state.

Adapter (the three EF repositories): operation = named read; observation = returned id sequence, loaded navigations and tracking state, statement count. Infrastructure: SQLite and Postgres through EF Core 10.0.14 / Npgsql 10.0.3; no timeout, retry, recovery or new failure path.

facts.F33: Formal verification: claim-to-checker mapping. Claims: (1) each named read returns the same rows, in the same order, with the same loaded graph as today's predicate on SQLite and Postgres; (2) no extra statements; (3) the S05a list shrinks. None is a state-transition, concurrency, liveness or recovery claim, so Quint and TLA+/TLC have nothing to model but a restatement, and an Agda proof would be about a model of LINQ, not EF's translation. Checker availability is INDETERMINATE: quint, java and agda were refused by the session shell allowlist (exit 126). Human waiver recorded by the maintainer at the DESIGN hold (2026-11-10): formal verification waived for claims (1)-(3); they stay INDETERMINATE as proofs; the executable evidence is the provider parity tests, RealityCheckQueryCountTest, the S05a guard and the metrics answer comparison. Install route if wanted: npm install -g @informalsystems/quint after allowing quint in the lean-ctx allowlist.
